newsitem.title: USA: Varlen Corp to redeem debentures for cash.
newsitem.headline: Varlen Corp to redeem debentures for cash.

text.p: Varlen Corp said on Tuesday it plans to redeem the company's 6.50 percent convertible subordinated debentures due 2003 for cash.
The principal amount of the debentures outstanding as of August 18 totaled $54,695,000.

They will be reedemed at a redemption price of $1,039.00 per $1,000.00 principal amount of the debentures plus accrued and unpaid interest of $16.79 to, but not including, the redemption date, for an aggretate cash redemption price of $1,055.79 per $1,000.00 principal amount of debentures.
Instead of a redemption, the debenture holders may elect to convert debentures into Varlen common stock prior to the close of business at 1700 EDT/2100 GMT on September 3, 1997, the company said.

The holders may convert the debentures into the company's common stock at a conversion price of $22.5893 per share, which equals about 44.2688 shares of common stock per $1,000.00 principal amount of debentures.

The company said it has entered into a standby purchase agreement under which the firms of Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp, Piper Jaffray Inc, and Robert W. Baird & Co Inc have agreed to purchase, at a predetermined price, the number of shares of common stock adequate to fund cash redemptions.
The number of shares the firms will purchase will be determined by the redemption price of the debentures that are not converted into the company's common stock.
If all of the debentures were converted into common stock, about 2.42 million additional common shares would be issued by the company.
Varlen has about 6.43 million shares outstanding.
(( Caryn Trokie, U.S. Corporate Bond Unit, 212-859-1678))
